summary: Configured /srv/drop on node1 as world-writable with the sticky bit (mode 1777, root:root), so any user can create files but only the owner (or root) can delete/rename them. Verified behaviorally with two test users both pre- and post-reboot, then performed the mandatory single-node restart with boot-identity proof and post-restart recovery verification.
actions_performed: Created /srv/drop and set mode 1777 (sticky bit) owned by root:root
Created two test users (dropuser1, dropuser2) and verified dropuser2 could write but not delete dropuser1's file (Operation not permitted), while the owner could delete their own file
Cleaned up test files and users (handled lingering systemd --user sessions via pkill before userdel)
Captured pre-restart baseline: boot_id, uptime -s, /srv/drop permissions, systemctl is-system-running
Issued `shutdown -r now` on node1 via backgrounded sudo command that returned acknowledgement before disconnect
Polled node1 until exec succeeded again after the reboot
Confirmed boot_id changed (dfdea52d... -> 5b01788d...) and uptime -s shifted, proving an actual restart occurred
Re-verified /srv/drop permissions persisted (1777 root:root) and re-ran the two-user sticky-bit behavioral test post-reboot, confirming cross-user delete is blocked and owner delete succeeds
Cleaned up post-reboot verification test users/files

evidence.requirement: /srv/drop exists, is shared/writable, with sticky bit preventing cross-user deletion
evidence.summary: chmod 1777 applied (stat shows 1777 root:root); dropuser1 wrote a file, dropuser2's rm was denied with 'Operation not permitted', dropuser2 could still write its own file, and each owner successfully deleted their own file afterward
Captured boot_id=dfdea52d..., uptime -s, /srv/drop mode 1777 root:root, and systemctl is-system-running=running before restart
Backgrounded `shutdown -r now` returned reboot_ack=0 before the node disconnected
Node became unreachable (connection timed out), then reachable again; new boot_id=5b01788d... (differs from pre-restart dfdea52d...) with new uptime -s, proving a genuine reboot

evidence.requirement: node1 post-restart recovery of required state/service
evidence.summary: After reboot, /srv/drop retained mode 1777 root:root, system reported running, and a fresh two-user test confirmed sticky-bit cross-user delete protection still functions correctly
